book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Price & Our Independent Verdict
question: What does Microsoft do, why is it priced at $523.88, and what is our exact action for new and existing capital?

epigraph.quote: In investing, what is comfortable is rarely profitable—and what is durable is rarely cheap unless the market is debating a transition.
epigraph.author: Institutional Research Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT) is the core operating system of global enterprise computing. Its platforms span Azure cloud infrastructure, Microsoft 365, Teams, LinkedIn, Dynamics 365, GitHub, and Xbox. In audited FY26, Microsoft generated $331,839 million in revenue (+17.8% YoY) and $155,237 million in operating income (46.8% margin) [4, 6]. Q1 FY27 revenue accelerated to $92.3 billion (+19% YoY) [5]. Azure surged +48% YoY, while commercial remaining performance obligations hit $677 billion (+73% YoY) [5, 19].

At $523.88 (27.36x trailing P/E, 21.71x forward P/E [26]), the market is debating cash conversion. FY26 free cash flow fell to $67,036 million (50.1% of net income) as AI capex surged to $115.9 billion [4, 20]. Management guided FY27 capex near $170 billion [19]. Yet our Reverse DCF shows $523.88 only prices in a 12.4% 10-year revenue CAGR, well below current 18.8% growth. On the chart, MSFT coils in a tight 7.47% volatility squeeze right on its 50-day SMA ($519.00) and 10-week EMA ($515.34). We assign IMMEDIATE_BUY for new capital ($660.00 base target, $452.41 stop, 1.90:1 CMP R:R). For the 7.6346 shares held in Charles Schwab ($3,999.61 value, 4.51% weight), our action is KEEP_COMPOUNDING (0 shares sold).

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — How to Read This Dossier
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 were written completely blind to Microsoft's stock price. You and I judged the business quality first without valuation bias. Only in Chapters 7 through 9 did we examine the $523.88 share price, the Stage 2 chart, and your 7.6346-share Schwab holding. That discipline ensures we underwrite an enduring compounder on its merits rather than rationalizing an existing position.

web_blocks.html: This dossier was built from scratch using primary SEC filings, official earnings releases, and same-session market ledgers. Pass 1 audited Microsoft's business quality and cash waterfall completely blind to stock prices and technicals. Pass 2 tested that locked fundamental reality against Reverse DCF, Stage 2 structure, and portfolio sizing rules. The result is a transparent, unhedged action plan with clear price and KPI triggers.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to the desk. Today you and I are underwriting Microsoft Corporation—not by glancing at a stock chart or repeating consensus headlines, but by tearing the business down to its studs first, completely blind to the share price, and only then confronting what Wall Street is charging for it.

In Chapters 1 through 6, we trace Microsoft's fifty-year journey from BASIC interpreters to a $331.8 billion revenue machine generating 46.8 percent operating margins and 24.2 percent returns on invested capital. We step inside actual enterprise deployments across Azure, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Xbox, and we follow every $100 of revenue down the cash waterfall to see why fiscal 2026 capital expenditures of $115.9 billion—and $170 billion guided for fiscal 2027—have cut free cash flow conversion in half to 50.1 percent.

In Chapters 7 through 9, we open the November 13, 2026 market ledger. At $523.88 per share, Microsoft trades at 21.7 times forward earnings—pricing in just 12.4 percent ten-year revenue growth even as Azure grows 48 percent and commercial backlog hits $677 billion. On the chart, while the Nasdaq-100 languishes below its 200-day moving average, Microsoft is coiling in a tight Stage 2 volatility squeeze right on top of its 50-day moving average.

Our independent verdict is unhedged: IMMEDIATE_BUY for new capital inside the $507.61 to $526.78 support zone, targeting $660.00 in the base case against a hard structural stop at $452.41. For your existing 7.6346 shares in Charles Schwab—worth $3,999.61, or 4.51 percent of the US portfolio—our action is KEEP_COMPOUNDING with zero shares sold, backed by clear exit and trim triggers.

Over the next nine chapters, we will test every assumption with primary filings, real customer deployments, and deterministic math. Whether you are evaluating your existing 7.6346-share Schwab stake or deciding where to put the next marginal dollar of US cash, you will finish this dossier with an unhedged, evidence-backed plan.

Notice what makes this setup intellectually honest rather than promotional. We are not ignoring the $170 billion fiscal 2027 capex bill, the 50.1 percent free cash flow conversion in fiscal 2026, or the April 2026 loosening of OpenAI exclusivity. Those are real risks that could pull the stock toward our $430.00 bear case if Azure monetization stumbles. Instead, we weigh those risks directly against a 21.7 times forward multiple, $677 billion in commercial RPO, and a Stage 2 chart coiled on institutional support.

Across our three investment horizons, the alignment is clear: short-term momentum shows a tight 7.47 percent Bollinger Band squeeze above the 50-day average; medium-term fundamentals hinge on Q2 FY27 Azure growth hitting 49 to 50 percent constant-currency guidance as delayed capacity comes online; and long-term compounding rests on a 24.2 percent ROIC enterprise platform with unmatched distribution.

Every number in this dossier is pulled from audited SEC filings, official Microsoft earnings releases, and same-session market ledgers as of November 13, 2026—built completely from scratch without relying on prior assumptions.
